title: Through the Iron Rafters
story:
Midday at the river port brought a deafening surge of activity. Wanting to push south beyond the town, James and Nico attempted to cut across the central shipping yard. The open asphalt lot was a terrifying grid of iron and motion. Yellow forklifts darted between towering stacks of wooden pallets, their backup beepers chirping frantically against the deep vibration of idling diesel engines. James clutched his small brass pocket compass to his chest as he and Nico darted between low supply crates.

Without warning, a massive flatbed truck reversed into their path. A heavy crane dropped a wooden crate of iron fittings onto the concrete barely two paces away, shaking the ground with a bone-rattling crash. Nico squeaked in terror and bolted toward a gap near the spinning rear tires. James lunged, catching his friend by his tail and pulling him back just as the heavy rubber tread rolled past. Squeezing under a stack of timber, James pressed his eyes shut and performed his grounding ritual, counting three distinct sounds—the hiss of air brakes, the clatter of a conveyor belt, and the high whine of a distant saw—until his racing pulse settled.

Once the immediate danger subsided, James scanned the yard for another way forward. The ground level was an unpredictable maze of heavy wheels, but high along the perimeter wall ran a suspended drainage pipe and an elevated catwalk framework. Climbing up an exterior drainage pipe, James carried Nico up into the overhead ironwork, far above the dangerous traffic. From this high vantage point, recovering from the scary encounter was easier, and a safe, elevated route through the yard presented itself along the steel rafters.

They moved carefully along the cool steel beams, stepping over rusted rivets until the noise of the machinery softened behind them. Descending a quiet access ladder near the southern gate, James and Nico stepped out onto the peaceful dirt shoulder of the southern road, leaving the industrial chaos of the river port behind.
location: Southern outskirts of San Antonio del Río
